In particular,  $ \gamma = k $ is an eigenvalue of  $ BB^{T} $ with multiplicity  $ \binom{n}{k} - \binom{n}{k-1} $. Also, we can verify that all nonzero eigenvalues of  $ BB^{T} $ and  $ B^{T}B $ are identical with the same multiplicities. Hence, for  $ j = 1, \ldots, k - 1 $,  $ B^{T}B $ has eigenvalue  $ \gamma = j $ with the same multiplicities  $ m(j) = m(\theta_{j}) $, also for  $ j = 0, 1, \ldots, k - 1 $,  $ B^{T}B $ has eigenvalue  $ \gamma = n - j + 1 $ with the same multiplicities  $ m(j) = m(\theta_{j}) $. In particular,  $ \gamma = k $ is an eigenvalue of  $ B^{T}B $ with multiplicity  $ \binom{n}{k} - \binom{n}{k-1} $.
